stories.headline: Hantavirus cruise ship MV Hondius evacuated at Tenerife amid political and intergovernmental tensions
stories.summary: The MV Hondius, a cruise ship with a hantavirus outbreak that killed three people, docked at Tenerife on May 10 after WHO and the EU asked Spain to manage the evacuation of 140+ passengers. Spanish authorities coordinated a major health and security operation; WHO Director-General Tedros arrived alongside multiple Spanish ministers. The crisis generated a sharp political dispute between the Canary Islands government (Clavijo) and central government (Sánchez), an intergovernmental row over competences at the port of Granadilla, and was weaponized by PP and Vox in the ongoing Andalusia election campaign.

stories.headline: Andalusia regional election campaign intensifies with Moreno (PP) as heavy favourite over PSOE's Montero
stories.summary: With the Andalusia regional election set for May 17, the final week of campaigning saw national leaders Sánchez and Feijóo rally alongside their respective candidates (Montero for PSOE, Moreno for PP-A), while polls showed PP on the cusp of retaining an absolute majority with Vox rising and PSOE heading for a historic low. Campaigns were disrupted by the hantavirus crisis and the Guardia Civil deaths but both major parties used those events as campaign fodder.

stories.headline: Two Guardia Civil officers killed pursuing drug boat in Huelva; government absence at funeral sparks political crisis
stories.summary: Two Guardia Civil agents (Germán and Jerónimo) died on May 9 while pursuing a drug-trafficking speedboat off the Huelva coast. Neither President Sánchez nor Interior Minister Marlaska attended the funeral, triggering sharp criticism from PP leader Feijóo, who demanded Marlaska's resignation and 'maximum-level accountability.' Vox's Abascal also attacked the government, continuing his campaign despite the official mourning. Sánchez expressed condolences at a campaign rally the following day.

stories.headline: Isabel Díaz Ayuso cuts Mexico trip short after controversy over Conquest remarks and Sheinbaum government pushback
stories.summary: Madrid regional president Ayuso's official visit to Mexico generated a diplomatic incident: her comments defending the Spanish Conquest and honouring Hernán Cortés clashed with the Mexican government's narrative, President Sheinbaum's office mobilized protests against her agenda, and Ayuso ultimately suspended the final stage of her trip, accusing Mexico of a 'boycott.' The episode intersected with King Felipe VI's earlier acknowledgement of 'abuses' during the Conquest and Spain-Mexico diplomatic normalisation efforts.

stories.headline: King Felipe VI attends Costa Rica presidential inauguration of Laura Fernández
stories.summary: King Felipe VI travelled to San José, Costa Rica to attend the May 8 inauguration of President-elect Laura Fernández (centre-right, Partido Pueblo Soberano), attending a dinner hosted by outgoing President Rodrigo Chaves and meeting with Guatemalan President Bernardo Arévalo and the Spanish community in Costa Rica. Foreign Minister Albares was notably absent, continuing a pattern of not accompanying the King on Iberoamerican trips.

stories.headline: Koldo/Ábalos corruption case expands: Aldama testimony threatens PSOE, Fiscalía requests Supremo declarations for Audiencia Nacional
stories.summary: Ongoing fallout from the 'trama Koldo' case: businessman Víctor de Aldama's defence announced he holds an 'arsenal' of incriminating evidence against PSOE figures including Congress president Armengol. The Fiscalía Anticorrupción asked the Audiencia Nacional to incorporate Koldo García and Aldama's Supremo testimony into its PSOE-financing investigation, and the presiding judge separately asked for those declarations. The case is linked to alleged corrupt contracts during the Ábalos-era Transport Ministry and potentially party financing.

stories.headline: CNI's Operation Kitchen trial: former director denies any intelligence agency involvement
stories.summary: The trial of the 'Operación Kitchen' — alleged PP-era espionage against former party treasurer Luis Bárcenas — entered its fifth week at the Audiencia Nacional. Former CNI director Félix Sanz Roldán (2009–2019) testified that the centre had 'zero absolute' involvement, calling participation illegal. Separately, the Barcelona Audiencia reopened a case into alleged Pegasus spying against Òmnium Cultural members, requesting the government to declassify CNI documents.

stories.headline: PP takes Lugo mayoralty via motion of censure backed by PSOE defector, ending 27 years of left-wing governance
stories.summary: The PP's Elena Candia became mayor of Lugo after a motion of censure passed with 13 votes — the PP's 12 councillors plus PSOE defector María Reigosa — against the incumbent PSOE-BNG coalition of 12. The operation had been facilitated by the deaths of two PSOE councillors whose seats were vacant. PSOE accused the PP of using its 'master class in transfugism.'

stories.headline: Sumar's rental moratorium decree fails in Congress; party reassesses coalition strategy and future leadership
stories.summary: Sumar's decree to extend rental price caps (moratorium on expired contracts through 2027) was rejected in Congress by votes of Junts, PP, and Vox, partly driven by a public dispute between Yolanda Díaz and Junts' Puigdemont. Sumar is exploring a revised proposal and trying to maintain influence within the coalition, while media speculate on Díaz's post-ministerial plans after she announced she will not stand in the next general election.

stories.headline: Banco de España LatAm Economic Forum: Escrivá warns on AI and cybersecurity; Lagarde rejects euro stablecoins
stories.summary: The Banco de España hosted the inaugural LatAm Economic Forum in Roda de Berà (Tarragona) on May 8–9 with 14 central bank governors and ECB President Lagarde. Governor Escrivá called for enhanced financial cybersecurity in the AI era and defended central bank trust as an anchor. Lagarde rejected stablecoins as a response to the digital dollar, citing systemic risks.

stories.headline: Pope León XIV's June Spain visit preparations under way; hantavirus raises last-minute scheduling uncertainty
stories.summary: Spain is preparing for Pope León XIV's apostolic visit from June 6–12, accepted by invitation of King Felipe VI and the Church. The Royal Family is expected to lead official reception in Madrid; the Pope will also travel to Barcelona. The Zarzuela Palace indicated the programme could be adjusted subject to WHO guidance in light of the hantavirus situation, while regional leaders including Basque President Pradales sought private audiences with the new Pontiff.

stories.headline: Death of Murcia mayor José Ballesta at 67 after cancer battle draws national tributes
stories.summary: PP mayor of Murcia José Ballesta died on May 10 at 67 after a prolonged battle with cancer. He was the longest-serving mayor of the city. PP leader Feijóo, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, and numerous national and regional figures offered tributes. A three-day official mourning was decreed by the Murcia city council.
